correctness.rationale: For three households at fixed total, relative Gini is exactly proportional to max-income minus min-income, while Theil T is ordered exactly by the integer product of each income raised to itself. Independent exhaustive partition generation proves the sharp total-13 finite boundary and uniqueness, and a separate calculus argument proves the infinite family for all integer x at least 6.

value.rationale: Gini and Theil are standard, policy-relevant inequality measures whose differing sensitivities motivate joint reporting. The smallest primitive equal-mean reversal is a natural exact benchmark for those differing judgments, and the infinite family proves that the effect is systematic rather than a one-off finite artifact.
